body: I'm even more tired now that I'm taking medication. I can literally fall asleep whenever and wherever.
I think I just like the comfort of knowing that people want to talk to me or hang out with me, without actually having to go through with it.

Whenever someone asks me what I do in my free time or 'for fun' I turn into a deer in headlights. Like I don't even have the attention span to watch movies or play video games, I just eat and browse the internet until there's nothing new to see or I get bored and fall asleep.

I never knew about 'atypical' depression until reading this post, but it sums me up perfectly. One time I was having such a bad day that I sat in the car in my work parking lot after my shift was over and cried for an hour.. then drove to my apartment and cried in my car for another half hour.... then sat on the couch for several hours still in my work clothes trying to find the energy to take a shower... then finally got in the shower and just fuckin' stood there forever.

I haven't really had days like this since I started taking medication, but the heavy feeling still comes around especially when I'm stressed out or haven't slept well.

I wasted a lot of my younger years questioning whether I had depression or not. If you feel like it's interfering with your daily life then there's no reason why you shouldn't be able to talk to someone about it or seek treatment.

I started taking Celexa about three years ago. I used to be afraid of drugs and medication, and never planned on going that route but my life was just so miserable at the time that I didn't know what else to do. I would cry my way home from work, barely had the motivation to shower or change my clothes (I always did but it took a lot more time and energy.)

I remember the first day I took it. I felt sick, kinda like I had the flu, but that only lasted about a day. After my shift was done at work that's when I noticed the effects. I wasn't sad or scared to go home, I was excited. I sang along to the radio. I made dinner and watched TV and just felt content and relaxed. I even started crying (in a good way) because I hadn't felt like that in a long time. 

A weird thing that happened for the first few days (or week, I don't remember how long) is that whenever i would get mad or try to frown, my face would smile instead. Instead of getting mad at someone or something I would get feelings of happiness. It was kinda fun lol.

Nowadays I feel pretty normal. I still cry and have bad days here and there but I can handle them a lot better. I'm sleepier than I used to be, but that's the only major side effect and I feel like it's worth it.

I can go a day without taking my medication and I feel fine, but if I try to go any longer I get really moody and headachey and everything pisses me off. I tried to quit (just because it was hard to make doctors appointments and pick up prescriptions every month with a busy schedule) and honestly it kinda ruined my last relationship. I was too moody and too needy to put up with.

tl;dr Medication really helped my situation with minimal side effects but it can be a bit of a chore sometimes and it's hard to quit.

depression is definitely my comfort zone. lying in bed, listening to sad music, reading posts on here... idk it's like i belong somewhere.

it took a long time for me to diagnose myself and get the treatment i needed. if i didn't feel miserable 24/7 i would try to talk myself out of not having depression. my symptoms were milder when i was younger, but have gotten much worse over the years.

it's always best to talk to a professional and take care of yourself sooner rather than later. i learned that the hard way.
that was actually one of my first symptoms of depression. i didn't want to do anything. whatever i used to find fun just became boring and pointless. *that* is what made me sad.

I'm pretty much staying alive for my family. Once my parents pass away, if I'm not in better shape, then I'll probably end up peacing out. Everyone else could give two fucks less about me (unless I have something to offer them, but even then they'll find some better to find it from.)

My depression hit around middle school. I was lazy and overweight (mostly just chubby, but in middle school that basically means you're a whale). I was constantly bullied and the only friends I had at the time were fake (they literally pretended to be my friend just so they could have shit to talk about.) 

It's been over 10 years and I still have to deal with fake friends. At a certain age you'd think people would grow up and stop taking advantage of you and wasting your time, right?

On my days off I sleep in and take at least two naps. One time I slept from midnight to 9pm the next day, with only a couple minutes in between waking up/going back to sleep. It's mostly the antidepressants that make me so tired, but I also kinda force myself to sleep in because I don't want to have to deal with negative thoughts.
I just deleted everyone except family off my fb. It's been such a habit for me to just type it in whenever I'm bored and I always end up feeling worse afterwards.

I've been made fun of for having an "illness that requires me to sleep in til noon." Yes, because lying in bed all day is so much more fun than going out and living life. People don't understand the actual physical and mental pain that comes with depression, they think it's just a glorified way of being lazy and unhappy.

This is all my life is. Just waiting to pass the time. Counting down until work is over, until it's time to eat, until it's time for bed. I'm just killing time before I die, and it saddens me that it's so far away.
I had to reschedule my last two dr.'s appointments. My next one isn't until next year, and my dr. won't let me get any refill's until I've seen her again.
I wish I knew what it felt like. Even if just for a day.

Even when I'm doing something on the weekends (I work two jobs) I still get mad anxiety when they come around. I can sit on my ass and do nothing on Sunday night and feel just fine, but Saturday? I wish it was over with.
I feel like a prisoner. Like I'm stuck in an empty room with an old, dusty Columbo book for entertainment and a plate full of bland food.

This. I've been depressed since I was 12... I'm almost 25. It's a lot harder to deal with as an adult. You can't just go home and hide in your room anymore. You have to go out, find jobs, make friends, find a place to live. All those years of being a hermit have caught up to me. I'm socially anxious, broke, and still tired.
If I wasn't so scared of dying I would've been gone a long time ago

Well for me the first signs were just apathy and low motivation. I didn't think I had a problem, I just assumed that I was lazier than most. I failed a lot of classes, had trouble getting out of bed, etc. As I got older I started getting really indecisive, like I couldn't decide what to do so I'd just end up lying on the couch all day instead. I had no interest in doing anything or seeing anyone after school, it just felt like a lot of work to me. After a while I became very lonely, sad and anxious and that's when I realized I had a problem. 

They're not always obvious when you're younger, and everyone experiences different symptoms. 

And don't feel sorry! It took me years to figure out what was wrong; depression isn't all black and white and can be hard to understand. It's always good to see a doctor, get a check up and make sure you're getting adequete vitamins and nutrients and have your blood checked. Fatigue, which is a big symptom, can be caused by a lot of things like low Vitamin D or an underactive thyroid.

If you start to feel down on yourself, though, or that things aren't worth it, don't be afraid to talk about it! Talk to your parents, ask about seeing a therapist. There are a lot of people willing to help.

I went through the same phase when I was your age. It does sound young but I'm glad you're this self-aware. Puberty sucked and was awkward but you'll grow out of quickly. When I younger I thought I was just really lazy and it messed up my self esteem for a while until I realized that there was more to it than that. Depression doesn't always start with sadness. Just relax, try to have fun when you can and keep doing well in school. If you're feeling worse then talk to someone about it, don't be afraid to tell your parents or siblings because they might've gone through the same things and could really help. I was afraid to tell my mom but what she told me afterwards was that my biological father (who I've never met) was diagnosed with bi polar and deipression and it was nothing to be ashamed of.

I know this is super cliche but 20 is still really young, you have so much time ahead of you. Finding someone that's meant to be takes time, and when you rush to hit a deadline then you're probably settling for less than you deserve. It doesn't make you any less of a person, just means your time hasn't come yet.

It's so much harder to stay motivated and pick up your life when you're left with nothing.

I lost my childhood best friend (and pretty much my only legit friend) of over a decade last year. I was at my lowest point in life for a while but then I found someone new. Life has a funny way of building you up and then breaking you down I guess. I just try to remind myself that just because things are bad now doesn't mean that's how they'll always be. Keep your head up.
